You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in space group number 59, Pmmn (Hall symbol −P 2ab 2a), using fractional atomic coordinates. The supplied input cell is orthorhombic, with lattice parameters a = 3.634684 Å, b = 6.324899 Å, c = 11.419331 Å, and all three interaxial angles equal to 90°. The declared input composition contains four vanadium atoms and ten oxygen atoms, for fourteen atoms in total. The input frame is related to the standard frame by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the matrix P is effectively the identity in the first two standard-frame components but reverses and reorders the third: its rows are (1, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), and (0, −1, 0), up to negligible numerical roundoff, and the origin shift s is (0.75, 0.75, 0). Thus the original input cell is recovered by applying the inverse of this exact frame relation rather than by assuming that the listed representative coordinates are already in the input setting.

In the standard Pmmn description, the vanadium sublattice consists of a single fourfold orbit on Wyckoff position 4e, with coordinate relation (1/4, y, z). Its representative atom lies at x = 0.25, y = 0.101123, and z = 0.083981, so the two independent positional parameters are y = 0.101123 and z = 0.083981; the remaining three members of the orbit are generated by the Pmmn symmetry operations.

Oxygen occupies three crystallographically independent sublattices. The first is the twofold Wyckoff position 2a, with coordinate relation (1/4, 1/4, z), represented by an oxygen atom at x = 0.25, y = 0.25, and z = 0.984881; here z = 0.984881 is the only independent coordinate. The second oxygen sublattice is a fourfold 4e orbit, again of the form (1/4, y, z), with representative position x = 0.25, y = 0.110163, and z = 0.336942, giving independent parameters y = 0.110163 and z = 0.336942. The third oxygen sublattice is another distinct fourfold 4e orbit, also following (1/4, y, z), but with representative coordinates x = 0.25, y = 0.5684, and z = 0.991355, so its independent parameters are y = 0.5684 and z = 0.991355. These two oxygen 4e orbits are inequivalent and must both be retained to reproduce the full O10 content together with the 2a orbit.

All positional values are quoted to six decimal places, matching the stated rounding precision, and no precision corrections are supplied. Accordingly, the listed coordinates are the final input geometry for this description: one V 4e orbit, one O 2a orbit, and two distinct O 4e orbits, arranged within the stated orthorhombic cell and related between input and standard settings by the explicit transformation given above.
